profiles.summary: Public Celo providers serve five execution builds, not two: forno and publicnode answer reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb (celo/reth-v1.0.9 or v1.0.10) and, for about one request in seven, the op-geth build c7ed55b8; stakely.io rotates 74cc8bb with 7680d6d (celo/reth-v1.0.0 or v1.0.1), 3cbf835 (v1.0.3) and 06140ff (v1.0.6 to v1.0.8). All of them run revm-interpreter 35.0.1. The three older reth builds lock ruint 1.18.0 or 1.20.0, and every build returned the specified word on every vector it was pinned to.

deltas.delta: The reth commit in the Celo version string is the celo-org/reth revision that each celo-kona release locks: 7680d6d in celo/reth-v1.0.0 and v1.0.1, 3cbf835 in v1.0.3, 6a0e4cf in v1.0.4, 1fc77b9 in v1.0.5, 06140ff in v1.0.6 to v1.0.8, 74cc8bb in v1.0.9 and v1.0.10. v1.0.0 to v1.0.3 lock ruint 1.18.0 and later tags 1.20.0. Every tag locks revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and revm-bytecode 10.0.0, from crates.io up to v1.0.9 and from celo-org/revm bd28f942 in v1.0.10.

stakely.io answers web3_clientVersion with four reth builds in rotation: 74cc8bb, 7680d6d, 3cbf835 and 06140ff. 1rpc.io/celo answered 7680d6d and then refused further requests for a usage limit. stakely.io also serves debug_traceTransaction, which forno, publicnode, ankr and drpc refuse.

deltas.delta: celo/reth-v1.0.4 changed a consensus rule without a fork: a CIP-64 transaction with a feeCurrency of twenty zero bytes is now an unregistered currency, where v1.0.0 to v1.0.3 treated it as native CELO. The builds 7680d6d and 3cbf835 still served by stakely.io predate the change.

The op-geth backend of forno (Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817, go1.24.13) answered 360 of 2,397 bracketed batches, and every one of the 215,637 vectors sent to it (battery, targeted set, cycle 27 edge set and large-index set) returned the specified word.

rpc.xlayer.tech and xlayerrpc.okx.com answer reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7; f60420a is the okx/reth revision locked by xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1, which builds revm-interpreter 37.0.3, revm-bytecode 11.0.1 and ruint 1.18.0 from crates.io. X Layer is the only network of the unit on ruint 1.18.0 at its main endpoint and on the 37.x interpreter, whose instructions now return a result instead of halting. The instruction files, the jump destination analysis and the ruint shift, byte, conversion and signed division paths were read, and all vector sets match.

deltas.delta: xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 locks okx/reth at f60420aaac6457295a38b66bd544bab28ab6ec5d (103 crates), while v0.0.7.3 and v0.0.7 lock 81573d2. The version string of the public endpoint therefore names the rc.1 build.

ruint 1.18.0 lacks the fixes of 1.20.0 (#603): wrong overflow flags of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr, shift amount truncation on 32 bit targets, and the big endian byte() bound. The shifted values were correct in every case. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 clamps the shift and byte index to below 256 and 32 before calling ruint and never reads those flags.
The X Layer mainnet hard fork of 10 November 2026 (op-node xlayer/v0.1.7 with xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3) completed; the status page lists no later scheduled upgrade.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on transaction boundaries. X Layer serves no debug traces on its public endpoints, so failed transactions were replayed with eth_call at the parent block.
Nothing new on the gas token or caps. Osaka is not active (CLZ is refused with NotActivated), so no EIP-7825 cap applies yet.

findings.title: Celo public endpoints answer from three superseded celo-reth releases, two of them older than a consensus fix
findings.difference: On Ethereum a provider endpoint normally names one current client. On Celo the stakely.io endpoint rotates four reth builds, three of them older releases: 7680d6d (celo/reth-v1.0.0 or v1.0.1), 3cbf835 (v1.0.3) and 06140ff (v1.0.6 to v1.0.8). Release v1.0.4 changed a consensus rule for CIP-64 transactions with a zero-address feeCurrency, so the two oldest builds would accept a block that current nodes reject.
findings.mechanism: A wallet, router or quoter that reads the PoolManager through such an endpoint gets an eth_call answer from whichever build serves that request. All four reth builds lock revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and either ruint 1.18.0 or 1.20.0, and each returned the specified word on every vector it was pinned to (7680d6d 214437 of 215637 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches; 3cbf835 4200 of 30108 large-index and edge vectors pinned before the run was stopped, 0 mismatches; 06140ff 3600 of 30108 large-index and edge vectors pinned before the run was stopped, 0 mismatches), so the PoolManager math (FullMath.mulDiv at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, TickMath at src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, TickBitmap.compress at src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:20-26) is computed the same on all of them. The builds differ in CIP-64 handling (zero-address feeCurrency before v1.0.4, fee-currency pricing of eth_call and eth_estimateGas before v1.0.5), which only changes simulated fees and acceptance of malformed CIP-64 transactions. Blocks come from the Celo sequencer, which runs a current build, so an old follower can only diverge if the sequencer itself includes such a transaction.
findings.impact: No PoolManager funds move and no withdrawal is blocked. A user relying on an old build may see a CIP-64 simulation priced differently from the chain, or a zero-address feeCurrency transaction accepted locally and then rejected.
findings.preconditions: The user's wallet or router uses stakely.io or another provider that still runs a pre v1.0.9 celo-reth build. Producing a divergent block needs the sequencer. The verifier saw only 74cc8bb and 7680d6d in 107 calls, so the rotation of 3cbf835 and 06140ff is unconfirmed. Release v1.0.4 also added the CIP-64 rule balanceOf(caller) >= gasLimit * maxFeePerGas.
findings.mitigations: Integrators should read the PoolManager through an endpoint that reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb or later and check web3_clientVersion; Celo can ask providers to retire builds older than v1.0.4.

Celo op-geth c7ed55b8: 215637 of 215637 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches (battery, targeted, extra and hiword together). A planted one-bit fault in three expected words was caught three times.

cleared.check: The three older reth builds on stakely.io (7680d6d, 3cbf835, 06140ff), each pinned the same way. 7680d6d got all four sets (215,637 vectors); 3cbf835 and 06140ff answer only about one request in eight to ten, so their four-set runs were stopped and a run of the edge and large-index sets (30,108 vectors) was stopped part way.

cleared.check: revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer) read against the edges OPCODES.md lists: shl, shr, sar, byte, signextend, div, sdiv, mod, smod, addmod, mulmod, exp, jump, jumpi, and the step loop that charges static gas before each instruction returns a result.
cleared.result: Shift amounts and byte indices go through usize::try_from with saturation and are compared with 256 and 32 before any ruint call (bitwise.rs:107-158); signextend acts only when the index is below 31 (arithmetic.rs:126-137); div and mod return zero for a zero divisor; i256_div returns MIN for MIN divided by minus one; jumpi tests the whole word. Since 35.0.1 the changes are the move from halt to a returned error and type renames; no arithmetic changed. ruint 1.18.0 try_from for usize rejects any value with a nonzero limb above the first (from.rs:704-721).
cleared.source: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-37.0.3.crate (src/instructions/bitwise.rs, arithmetic.rs, i256.rs, control.rs, interpreter.rs:295-321) and https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.18.0.crate (src/bits.rs:325-480, src/from.rs:704-721)

cleared.check: ruint fixes after the versions these chains lock (1.18.0 on X Layer and Celo v1.0.0 to v1.0.3, 1.20.0 on later Celo tags) that touch EVM arithmetic: #603 (shift flags, 32 bit truncation, byte bound), #666 (div_3x2_ref), #681 (mul_mod of 1.21.0).
cleared.result: #603 changed flags and 32 bit truncation only; revm reads no shift flag and calls the shifts with amounts below 256. #666 fixed a reference function the library division does not use (it uses div_3x2_mg10, per the PR text). #681 is the 1.21.0 fault that neither chain locks. No fix reaches a value FullMath, TickMath, BitMath, SqrtPriceMath or TickBitmap computes, and the vectors aimed at each shape pass on both chains.

cleared.check: Jump destination analysis: revm-bytecode 10.0.0 (Celo) and 11.0.1 (X Layer) against the newest release 43.0.0, and the PoolManager runtime tail.
cleared.result: 10.0.0 and 11.0.1 have the same analysis.rs. 43.0.0 only replaces a pointer add past the end with wrapping_add for a trailing truncated PUSH and has no vector kernels. The deployed 24,009 byte runtime on both chains ends without a truncated PUSH and has 610 JUMPDEST bytes outside push data, so the changed line is never reached for it.

cleared.result: A linear scan of the 24,009 byte runtime read from Celo has no byte outside push data that is unassigned under Cancun. CLZ (0x1e) is refused with NotActivated on celo-reth and X Layer and answers 0xf8 on Ethereum for input 0xff.

Lagoon lists only OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink and Soneium for 11 January 2027, and its post-execution code on X Layer is gated after Karst (cycle 22). leads.question: On stakely.io, which serves debug_traceTransaction, does a CIP-64 transaction with a clearing debit and a refill in the main call show gasUsed equal to gross minus gross/5 (F-144)?
leads.why: It would confirm F-144 on a mined transaction; this cycle found a trace source but the candidate search did not close it.

leadResults.answer: Both sets returned the specified word on X Layer f60420a (hiword 15510 of 15510 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches; extra 14598 of 14598 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches), on Celo reth 74cc8bb (30108 of 30108 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches) and on the Celo op-geth build (215637 of 215637 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches with battery and targeted), each eth_call bracketed in one batch by web3_clientVersion. The three older reth builds on stakely.io gave the same: 7680d6d 214437 of 215637 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches, 3cbf835 4200 of 30108 large-index and edge vectors pinned before the run was stopped, 0 mismatches, 06140ff 3600 of 30108 large-index and edge vectors pinned before the run was stopped, 0 mismatches.

Pinned one batch at a time, Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 answered 360 of 2,397 batches and returned the specified word for battery, targeted, extra and the 15,510 large-index vectors (215637 of 215637 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches). reth 74cc8bb returned them too (30108 of 30108 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches for the large-index and edge sets; battery and targeted on forno 0 mismatches).

Karst still has no Celo notice or time, and the newest celo-kona tag is still celo/reth-v1.0.10 (revm 38 fork). 0x4200..0029 to 0x4200..002C hold the 2,059 byte proxy with implementation slot zero and balance zero at block 83,829,596. The post-activation sweep stays open.

No celo-reth tag carries revm 42.0.1 yet. The build reth/v2.2.0-7680d6d is celo/reth-v1.0.0 or v1.0.1 (both lock celo-org/reth 7680d6d, revm-interpreter 35.0.1 from crates.io, ruint 1.18.0); it is also served by 1rpc.io and stakely.io, and pinned on stakely it returned 214437 of 215637 vectors pinned, 0 mismatches. The revm 42 rerun stays open.

f60420a is the okx/reth revision locked 103 times by xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 (v0.0.7.3 locks 81573d2), so the endpoint runs the rc.1 tag, whose deps/optimism submodule cycle 25 read as a492b62 (L-1022) with handler and EVM files equal to xlayer/v0.1.7.

revm-bytecode 43.0.0 (26 August 2026), the newest release on crates.io, has no vector kernels: legacy/analysis.rs is scalar and only gained wrapping_add for a trailing PUSH. Celo locks 10.0.0 and X Layer 11.0.1, which share analysis.rs. No release carries the kernels yet.

stakely.io now serves debug_traceTransaction for Celo, so a trace source exists. In the newest 20,000 blocks 88,455 of 175,626 transactions were CIP-64 and none had a parent-block fee-currency balance equal to its maximum debit (gas limit times max fee); 5273 had a balance within twice the debit, 5,266 of them in one currency (0x0e2a3e05). The scan does not model balance changes earlier in the same block or adapter scaling, so a clearing debit could still have been missed. No traced example was found and F-144 stays confirmed from source only.

Celo: in the newest 30,000 blocks forno returned 12,221 failed receipts; the newest 1,500 were traced with callTracer on stakely.io (112 trace errors) and 3 entered the PoolManager. One reverted inside unlock with selector 0xe39aafee, which is not an error declared in src/; unlock calls the caller's unlockCallback as a high level call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) and passes that revert up, so it is a revert of the caller's own callback, with 265,396 of 305,439 gas used. Two read the PoolManager with extsload and reverted later in the caller with empty data. Only 35 transactions in that window were sent straight to the PoolManager, PositionManager or a Universal Router, none failed. X Layer, which serves no traces: in the newest 30,000 blocks 484,418 receipts held 396 transactions sent straight to the PoolManager or its periphery and none failed. No failed transaction on either chain points to a PoolManager result that differs from the source; transactions entering through other routers on X Layer were not searched, because a failed receipt cannot be tied to the PoolManager without a trace.
